rules.statement: Use text for links in most cases.
heading_path: Link to something only if it helps meet the user’s need
rules.violation_condition: An image is used as a link where text would meet the need and there is no user need for using the image.

rules.statement: Place this after the title in roman type and enclosed in parentheses.
heading_path: Broadcast media and podcasts (film, video, television and radio programs)
Use italics and sentence case for film titles
rules.violation_condition: The title of a film, television program, radio program, podcast series or published script is not italicised.
compliant_examples: A local podcast in this popular genre is Australian true crime, hosted by Meshel Laurie and Emily Webb.
Peter Carey and Ray Lawrence co-wrote Bliss: the screenplay.
Gruen is a popular television program on ABC TV.
You can read David Knox’s review of The gloaming on TV Tonight.
Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975) helped to revive the Australian film industry in the 1970s.
Environmentalists will enjoy the radio program Off track on ABC Radio National.

rules.statement: Don't use a full stop, comma or semicolon after an ellipsis.
heading_path: Show missing words or ideas with ellipses
rules.violation_condition: An ellipsis is followed by a full stop, comma or semicolon.
compliant_examples: I’ve written hundreds of reports: annual reports, white papers …!
The review clarified that the Army might have to fight on home ground … To be properly equipped, the Army needs a new troop carrier.

rules.statement: Use initial capitals for these terms when referring to specific legislation:
heading_path: Use initial capitals for formal names and titles
rules.violation_condition: ‘Act’ is lower case in a legislative reference, or ‘Bill’, ‘Regulation’ or ‘Ordinance’ has casing inconsistent with whether the reference is specific or generic.
compliant_examples: The bills were rejected for the second time.
The Act separated legal ties between the 2 entities.

rules.statement: Square brackets with an italicised 'sic' show that the error in the text is from the original writer.
heading_path: Use square brackets to show insertions in quotes
rules.violation_condition: A marker identifying an error as belonging to the original writer is not written as italicised ‘sic’ enclosed in square brackets.
compliant_examples: Written late at night, the report began, ‘The office was previously in Melberne [sic].’

rules.statement: Retain any post-nominals for civil and military honours when using the shortened forms of titles.
heading_path: Write post-nominals after the name in academic and professional titles
Include post-nominals in the shortened forms of titles
rules.violation_condition: A shortened presentation of an individual’s title drops applicable civil or military honour post-nominals.
compliant_examples: Attendees: Dr Z Switkowski AO, Prof M Bean CBE, Dr S Andrews, Ms J Latchford, Prof S Duckett, Ms T McLaughin and Mr D Hoogstra.

rules.statement: You must still refer to the table in the body of the text.
heading_path: Use tables if they make content easier to read
rules.violation_condition: A table has no reference to it in the body text.

rules.statement: Place a comma between the title of the work and the first division.
heading_path: Include divisions in in-text citations when possible
rules.violation_condition: The title-to-division boundary lacks a comma when divisions are spelled out, or contains a comma in a subsequent citation using division numbers alone.

rules.statement: Don't follow 'e.g.' or 'i.e.' with a comma, regardless of whether you would use a comma in the sentence.
heading_path: Avoid using Latin shortened forms in most content
rules.violation_condition: A comma immediately follows ‘e.g.’ or ‘i.e.’.

rules.statement: Avoid using Latin shortened forms in most content
heading_path: Avoid using Latin shortened forms in most content
rules.violation_condition: A Latin shortened form appears instead of English without an applicable special-use context, or ‘etc.’ is used despite the specific instruction against it.
compliant_examples: The department has a major problem with its website – that is, users find pages are very slow to load.
This funding is intended for upgrading roads in Gold Coast and Hinterland urban centres (for example, Surfers Paradise and Southport).
They found some aspects of grammar confusing – for example, the different types of pronouns.
This funding is for upgrading roads in the Gold Coast and Hinterland urban centres (Surfers Paradise, Southport, Upper Coomera and Robina).
violating_examples: The department has a major problem with its website, i.e. users find pages very slow to load.
They found some aspects of grammar confusing, e.g. the different types of pronouns.
This funding is for upgrading roads in Gold Coast and Hinterland urban centres (for example, Surfers Paradise, Southport etc.).

rules.statement: Don't use full stops in:
heading_path: Write headings, measurements and captions without full stops
rules.violation_condition: A punctuation full stop occurs in a heading, stand-alone list, or page header or footer, or is added after a caption or title.

rules.statement: Open with 'Dear Minister'.
heading_path: Address certain office holders of the Australian Parliament as ‘Honourable’
The presiding officers and former office holders of state parliaments
rules.violation_condition: Correspondence to one of the specified office holders lacks the opening appropriate to the recipient’s office and the stated level of formality.

rules.statement: Place modifying words, such as adjectives and adverbs, next to the thing that they're modifying.
heading_path: Sentence structure sets the function of words
rules.violation_condition: A modifying word, phrase or clause is not next to the word or expression it is intended to modify.
compliant_examples: Jamilah only told Freddie that she respected him.
Jamilah told Freddie that she only respected him.
Jamilah told Freddie only that she respected him.
Jamilah told Freddie that she respected only him.
Jamilah told Freddie that only she respected him.
Jamilah told only Freddie that she respected him.
Only Jamilah told Freddie that she respected him.
The report suggested that the drug is beneficial, even though it’s harmful in larger doses.
violating_examples: Even though it’s harmful in larger doses, the report suggested the drug is beneficial.

rules.statement: Indirect questions and commands don’t use a question mark
heading_path: Indirect questions and commands don’t use a question mark
rules.violation_condition: An indirect question, command or instruction is punctuated with a closing question mark.
compliant_examples: Please upload your edits.
Consider who your future colleagues might be.

rules.statement: In this case, the name and date appear in parentheses after the genus and species name.
heading_path: Refer to classification systems to help you name plants and animals
Scientific names can include the name of a person
rules.violation_condition: For a species transferred to a different genus, an included original-authority credit is not enclosed in parentheses after the genus and species name.

rules.statement: Follow normal sentence structure in each list item.
heading_path: Use sentence lists for a series of complete sentences
rules.violation_condition: An item presented as part of a sentence list is not a grammatically complete sentence.

rules.statement: Use 70 characters or fewer
heading_path: Write headings that are clear and short
rules.violation_condition: A heading contains more than 70 characters, counting spaces.

rules.statement: Address a judge who is a knight or dame as 'The Honourable Sir' or 'The Honourable Dame'.
heading_path: Use the correct form to refer to judges and magistrates
rules.violation_condition: A formal address of a judge who is a knight or dame lacks the applicable ‘The Honourable Sir’ or ‘The Honourable Dame’ form, other than a permitted subsequent mention.
compliant_examples: The Honourable Dame Roma Flinders Mitchell AC DBE CVO QC
Sir Ninian
Dame Roma
The Honourable Sir Ninian Stephen KG AK GCMG GCVO KBE QC

rules.statement: In a reference list, put the family name first and then the initial for the given name of the lead author.
heading_path: List family name first in reference lists
rules.violation_condition: A reference-list entry gives the lead author's name in an order or form other than family name followed by given-name initials.

rules.statement: Use the generic names of drugs where possible.
heading_path: Cite common names for pharmaceutical drugs, not brand names
rules.violation_condition: A drug is referred to by its brand name instead of an available generic or common name.
compliant_examples: benzoyl peroxide (Benzac)
paracetamol (Panadol)

rules.statement: Rule: Creator C (Year) 'Title of song: subtitle of song' [Medium], Title of compilation or album, Name of Publisher.
heading_path: Include musical compositions if you’re using a reference list
rules.violation_condition: An author–date reference-list entry for a song does not follow the stated sequence and bibliographic punctuation for creator, year, song title, medium, containing album or compilation, and publisher.
compliant_examples: Tones and I (2019) ‘Dance monkey’ [Song], The kids are coming, Sony Music Australia.

rules.statement: Use italics for the formal title of a complete published work.
rules.violation_condition: A complete published work's formal title is not italicised, or a component title such as an article or chapter is italicised instead of remaining non-italic.
compliant_examples: J Mackenzie, The editor’s companion, 2nd edn, Cambridge University Press, Melbourne, 2011.

rules.statement: Include the title, date and page number at the top or bottom of the page.
rules.violation_condition: A page of a print periodical without a separate cover lacks the title, date or page number in its header or footer.

rules.statement: Separate divisions with a comma.
heading_path: Include divisions in in-text citations when possible
rules.violation_condition: Multiple divisions are separated with punctuation other than commas in a first citation, or other than full stops in a subsequent numeric citation.

rules.statement: When you write to or about people, always use the form of personal name that the person uses.
rules.violation_condition: A person is referred to by a name, spelling or ordering of names that does not match the form they use.

rules.statement: Rule: Source: Adapted from Source (Year).
heading_path: Sequence the elements of online sources
rules.violation_condition: A source note for an adapted table or figure does not use the ‘Source: Adapted from’ identification followed by the source and year.
compliant_examples: Source: Adapted from MDBA (2019).

rules.statement: No space or full stop.
rules.violation_condition: The shortened million suffix ‘m’ is separated from the amount by a space or is written with an abbreviation full stop.

rules.statement: When you create a title, use 4 digits for the first year and 2 digits for the second year.
heading_path: Follow exceptions to the general rule
Use an en dash for a date span in titles of publications and programs
rules.violation_condition: A newly created publication or program title uses a year span without an en dash or with year lengths other than the prescribed 4-digit start and 2-digit end, subject to the century and house-style exceptions.

rules.statement: Avoid using shortened forms in headings
heading_path: Write all headings in sentence case and use minimal punctuation
Avoid using shortened forms in headings
rules.violation_condition: A heading contains a shortened form that is not better known than its full term, or an abbreviation whose meaning is unclear in an organisation-required all-capital heading.

rules.statement: Rule: A Author, 'Title of paper: subtitle of paper' [conference presentation], Name of Conference, Place of Conference, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
heading_path: Reference all elements of online sources
rules.violation_condition: A conference-paper reference omits the presentation designation, conference name or conference location, or fails to distinguish an unpublished presentation.

rules.statement: Always capitalise 'Constitution' when writing about Australia's Constitution.
heading_path: Reference to Australia’s Constitution needs capitalisation only
rules.violation_condition: The word ‘constitution’ has a lower-case initial when referring to Australia’s Constitution.

rules.statement: Use initial capitals for the full names of:
heading_path: Use initial capitals for formal names and titles
rules.violation_condition: A full or still-specific abbreviated name of a government program, treaty, protocol or similar agreement lacks its required capitals, or a generic reference unnecessarily retains capitals.
compliant_examples:
the Greater Artesian Basin Sustainability Initiative
the Artesian Basin Initiative
the initiative

rules.statement: Use numerals for 2 and above in text
heading_path: Use numerals for 2 and above in text
rules.violation_condition: An ordinary number is written in words when it is 2 or greater, or as a numeral when it is zero or one, outside the stated exceptions.
compliant_examples: They were open to discussing 3 options.
Only one person agreed to it.
Their aim is zero net emissions by 2050.
violating_examples: They were open to discussing three options.
Their aim is 0 net emissions by 2050.

rules.statement: Use 2 non-breaking spaces to keep each name together on one line of text.
heading_path: Refer to specific days, events and periods with capitals
rules.violation_condition: A full world-war name has breakable spaces between its three components.

rules.statement: When someone has a military rank and another title such as 'Sir', 'Dame' or 'the Honourable', place the military rank first.
heading_path: Address members of the ADF by rank, name and post-nominals
Write the rank before the title of ADF members who are knighted
rules.violation_condition: An ADF member’s non-military title precedes their military rank.
compliant_examples: General Sir John Monash GCMG KBE VD

rules.statement: As far as possible, avoid using forward slashes either side of a line break.
heading_path: Don’t add spaces around most forward slashes
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash directly beside an avoidable print line break, or a slash placed after the line break when the split is unavoidable.

rules.statement: Rule: A Author, 'Title of article: subtitle of article', Name of Journal, in press.
heading_path: Reference all elements of online sources
Journal article accepted for publishing, but not yet published
rules.violation_condition: A citation to a journal article accepted but not yet published omits ‘in press’ or presents it as an already published article.

rules.statement: repeat information in the alt text that a user would read in the caption
heading_path: Alt text, captions and titles for images
Give all users access to the same information
rules.violation_condition: An image’s alt text duplicates information in its caption, causing the same information to be read twice.

rules.statement: You should not use slang when writing on behalf of government.
heading_path: Choose how formal tone should be
rules.violation_condition: Slang appears in writing on behalf of government.

rules.statement: Never use an emoji in formal correspondence.
heading_path: Structure the body to help the user
rules.violation_condition: Formal correspondence contains an emoji, or informal correspondence uses an emoji inappropriate to its context.

rules.statement: Always use the short title in italics the first time you cite the Act in your text.
heading_path: Style for Act titles is title case, not always italics
After first mention, use the short title in roman type without the year
rules.violation_condition: The first in-text citation of an Australian Act uses its long title instead of its short title, or presents its short title without italics.
compliant_examples: The Currency Act 1965 established the Royal Australian Mint to produce Australia’s circulating coins. The Act also sets restrictions on amounts that can be paid in coins as ‘legal tender’.

rules.statement: Include the recipient's name and postal address at the top of the letter.
heading_path: Confirm privacy rules before you write to someone
rules.violation_condition: A letter lacks the recipient’s name or postal address at the top, or its address block omits the additional organisational details required for a recipient in an organisation.

rules.statement: Write these 'borrowed' words without italics or accent marks.
heading_path: Set off most foreign words and phrases
rules.violation_condition: An accent mark is retained in a word or phrase used as an assimilated Standard Australian English borrowing.

rules.statement: Address chaplains and maritime spiritual wellbeing officers by title
heading_path: Address chaplains and maritime spiritual wellbeing officers by title
rules.violation_condition: An ADF chaplain or maritime spiritual wellbeing officer is addressed by military rank instead of their applicable chaplaincy or MSWO title.
compliant_examples: Chaplain Catherine Inches-Ogden CSC
Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer Tammy Dunne
Principal Air Chaplain Kevin Russell CSC GAICD
Senior Chaplain Brian Rayner OAM RAN
Principal Chaplain Darren Jaensch
Principal Chaplain Darren Jaensch [Army]

rules.statement: Rule: I Interviewer, Interviewer Full Name interviews Interviewee Full Name: Title of interview [interview transcript], Name of Publisher, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
heading_path: Reference all elements of online sources
rules.violation_condition: An interview citation fails to lead with the interviewer, omits the interviewer–interviewee identification or format designation, or uses the interviewee rather than interviewer in a short citation.

rules.statement: don't use italics.
heading_path: Don’t write brands or types of vehicles in italics
rules.violation_condition: A vehicle brand, model or class name is italicised.

rules.statement: Organise ideas into short paragraphs.
heading_path: Design headings and other elements to help the user scan the page
rules.violation_condition: Ideas are packed into an overlong paragraph rather than divided into short paragraphs.

rules.statement: Unless advised in this manual, avoid using capitals in body text for a particular position or role within an organisation. This practice goes against readability and does not support clarity.
heading_path: Follow the guidance on capitals for titles and government terms
rules.violation_condition: a position or role within an organisation capitalised in body text without preceding a name

rules.statement: Write clear page titles.
heading_path: Structure content to help the user to navigate and understand
rules.violation_condition: A page title is vague or misleading about the page's subject or purpose.

rules.statement: Make sure you use the correct form.
heading_path: Comparison with adverbs is by degree
rules.violation_condition: A comparative or superlative adjective form is used where an adverb form is required, such as ‘quickest’ instead of ‘most quickly’.
compliant_examples: Tom speaks more quickly than Bob, but Harry speaks the most quickly of them all.
Bob spoke more quickly than Tom.
You finished work early, but they finished even earlier.
He spoke well, but she spoke better.
